title: Label review surgery — workshop notes & adjudication protocol
body:
Purpose:
This is a working write-up from the 2025-11-03 label-review “surgery” workshop. Goal: produce a compact adjudication protocol + quick-reference rubric for onboarding new annotators and for spot-check regression reviews during model rollouts. This doc mixes formal guidance, real sample cases from the workshop, and open questions we should resolve before finalizing the playbook.

High-level rules (TL;DR):
- Favor reproducibility over nuance: if two reasonable labelers disagree, annotate as NEUTRAL/AMBIGUOUS and escalate for adjudication.
- Prefer explicit rationale: every non-obvious vote must include a 1–2 line justification.
- Use three-way labels where helpful: ACCEPT / REJECT / AMBIGUOUS. For safety-sensitive classes use more granular tags (SAFE/UNSAFE/POLICY-UNCLEAR).

Definitions used in this repo and workshop:
- Labeler: human annotator running the prompt set and assigning a label.
- Adjudicator: senior reviewer who resolves disagreements and writes the final rationale.
- Case: a single prompt + model output + metadata (model version, seed, temperature).
- Tag: free-text or from canonical list (e.g., hallucination, factual-error, toxic, style-violation).

Label schema (recommended for onboarding evals):
- Primary: {ACCEPT, REJECT, AMBIGUOUS}
- Error tags (0..n): {HALLUCINATION, FACTUAL_ERROR, INCOMPLETE_ANSWER, POLICY_VIOLATION, OFF_TOPIC, UNRESPONSIVE}
- Confidence: {HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW}
- Rationale: short sentence (mandatory if label != ACCEPT OR confidence != HIGH)

Adjudication flow (practical):
1) Dual-labeling: two independent labelers annotate each case.
2) Auto-pass: if both labelers agree on label & tags AND both confidence HIGH -> case closed.
3) Soft-dispute: if label differs OR tags differ -> send to adjudicator queue.
4) Adjudicator action: pick final label + canonicalize tags + write 1–3 sentence rationale. If adjudicator finds systematic ambiguity, they add a clarification to the prompt-set doc and kick off a mini-review.
5) Logging: every adjudication must reference the original annotator IDs, timestamps, and the adjudicator rationale.

Adjudicator heuristics (quick checks):
- If output contains fabricated facts not supported by prompt context -> tag HALLUCINATION and usually REJECT.
- If output misreads the question but attempts an answer -> tag INCOMPLETE_ANSWER; can be AMBIGUOUS if partial credit applies.
- Safety violations -> immediate REJECT and tag POLICY_VIOLATION; escalate to safety lead for borderline cases.
- Style/format issues (e.g., wrong format but correct content) -> prefer ACCEPT + tag STYLE_VIOLATION if content is correct and retrain formatting.

Inter-annotator agreement (IAA) heuristics we trialed:
- Metrics: Cohen’s Kappa (binary), Krippendorff’s alpha (multi-class), pairwise percent agreement.
- Thresholds for operational acceptability (workshop consensus):
  - Percent agreement >= 0.80 and Kappa >= 0.60 -> OK for production sampling.
  - Percent agreement 0.65–0.80 or Kappa 0.40–0.60 -> needs focused calibration and targeted adjudication.
  - Percent agreement < 0.65 or Kappa < 0.40 -> pause rollout, run calibration sprint (2 days).
- Notes: Kappa will deflate on rare labels; track class-level F1 to catch imbalanced failure modes.

Sample calculation (toy):
- 200 cases, label set {ACCEPT, REJECT, AMBIGUOUS}
- Observed agreement: 156/200 = 0.78
- Expected agreement (marginals) = 0.49 -> Cohen’s kappa = (0.78 - 0.49)/(1 - 0.49) = 0.57 -> interpret as moderate agreement; plan calibration.

Workshop examples (redacted):
Case A: Prompt: "Summarize policy X for a non-technical user." Model: v3a, temp 0.2. Output includes an invented timeline.- Annotator1: REJECT, tags=[HALLUCINATION], confidence=HIGH, rationale="Invented dates not in prompt."- Annotator2: AMBIGUOUS, tags=[HALLUCINATION, TONE_ISSUE], confidence=MEDIUM, rationale="Mostly correct but I think timeline is fabricated."- Adjudicator: REJECT, tags=[HALLUCINATION], rationale="Fabricated factual claim changes user guidance; reject."

Case B: Prompt: "Give three quick tips to reduce cost of GPU inference." Model: v3b, temp 0.0. Output gives two correct tactics + one generic line "try different hardware" with no actionable steps.- Annotator1: ACCEPT, tags=[INCOMPLETE_ANSWER], confidence=MEDIUM, rationale="Two solid tips; last tip too vague but might be okay."- Annotator2: REJECT, tags=[INCOMPLETE_ANSWER], confidence=MEDIUM, rationale="Third tip is vacuous; overall answer incomplete."- Adjudicator: AMBIGUOUS, tags=[INCOMPLETE_ANSWER], rationale="Two useful items, one weak—mark ambiguous and add to prompt-set notes for clearer expectations on 'actionable' content."

Adjudicator notes template (use this to speed edits):
- Case id: <id>
- Model: <model+version>
- Original labels: A1=<label> (rationale), A2=<label> (rationale)
- Final: <label> 
- Tags: <canonical tags>
- Short rationale (1–3 lines): <why final choice>
- Follow-ups: {update prompt-set, retrain annotators, escalate to safety, sample more cases}

Calibration exercises (recommended cadence):
- Weekly: 50 mixed-difficulty spot cases pulled from last week’s production traffic; all labelers do these as a group. Review results in 90-minute session.
- Quarterly: 500-case calibration with new hires + adjudicators; compute Kappa and class-wise confusion matrices.
- Pre-rollout: For any model variant promoted to prod, run a 1000-case regression test; require Kappa > 0.5 OR documented mitigation plan.

Common failure modes and remediation notes:
- Drift in prompt understanding: add short clarifying bullets to the prompt-set doc; examples + counterexamples help.
- Ambiguous acceptance criteria: convert vague accept/partial rules into binary checks (e.g., "contains at least 2 concrete steps -> ACCEPT").
- Tag proliferation: maintain canonical tag list; adjudicators may map free-text tags into canonical ones during adjudication.

Open questions & TODOs (from workshop):
- Q1: Should we allow a 4th adjudicator vote (tie-breaker) or rely solely on the senior adjudicator? (action: Priya to prototype metric where 10% of adjudicated cases are double-audited).
- Q2: Where to surface confidence at the model level vs. labeler level in dashboards? (action: Ethan to design dashboard mockups).
- Q3: Formalize mapping from free-text tags -> canonical taxonomy (action: Maya to propose mapping by 2025-11-17).

Quick reference for new annotators (one-pager style):
- If output invents facts -> REJECT + HALLUCINATION.
- If answer is partially correct but missing key steps -> AMBIGUOUS + INCOMPLETE_ANSWER.
- Safety or policy concern -> REJECT + POLICY_VIOLATION, notify safety lead.
- Formatting or tone issues only -> ACCEPT + STYLE_VIOLATION (unless format is required by prompt).

Notes to self (raw, keep for iteration):
- Consider adding short inline checkboxes in labeling UI for common errors to improve downstream analytics (counts per tag, time to adjudicate).
- Track median time-to-adjudication; target < 48 hours for production-critical pipelines.
- Save a small corpus of edgecases for weekly "edgecase of the week" training.

Appendix: minimal JSON schema for exported annotations (for engineers):
- id: string
- model: string
- prompt: string
- output: string
- annotator_id: string
- label: {ACCEPT|REJECT|AMBIGUOUS}
- tags: [string]
- confidence: {HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW}
- rationale: string
- timestamp: ISO8601
- adjudicator_id: string/null
- adjudicated_label: {ACCEPT|REJECT|AMBIGUOUS}/null
- adjudicator_rationale: string/null

End of notes — next step: consolidate canonical tags and ship a 10-case quick-start for new annotators by 2025-12-01.

(Unresolved: finalize Kappa threshold for pre-rollout, see open Qs above.)
